resources.string: A floating button that takes a screenshot, lets you mark it up and shares it.
ClaudeShot needs to display over other apps so its button can float on every screen. In the list that opens, pick ClaudeShot and turn on “Allow display over other apps”.
ClaudeShot can display over other apps.
If Android says it’s a restricted setting: open App info, tap ⋮ at the top right, choose “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Allow display over other apps first (above).
Turn it on to keep a screenshot button floating on every screen.
Tap it on any screen to take a screenshot. The first time, Android asks to allow screen capture. Tap “Start”.
The button always stays fully visible.
After a few seconds the button turns see-through, so it hides less of the screen.
After a few seconds the button fades and slides half off the edge. Tap it once to bring it back, then tap again for a screenshot.

Android keeps Power + Volume down for itself, so no app can take those keys over. Turn this on and every screenshot you take with them opens straight in the ClaudeShot editor. Your phone still saves the original to its Screenshots album.
The floating button shows up in screenshots taken with the phone buttons. Pick “Tuck in” above, or turn the button off, if that bothers you.
ClaudeShot needs access to your photos to see new screenshots. Turn this on again, or allow Photos in App info.
You allowed only some photos. To catch new screenshots, open App info → Permissions → Photos and videos, and choose “Allow all”.
ClaudeShot can’t see new screenshots without access to your photos.

On: screenshots are instant after you allow screen capture once. Android shows a screen-sharing icon while the button is on, and asks again after you lock your phone. Off: Android asks before every screenshot.
Tap the floating button to take a screenshot. It opens in the editor.
Mark it up with Pen, Marker, Arrow, Box and Text. Use Blur to hide private details and Crop to keep just the part you need.
Copy, Save or Share from the top bar. Saved screenshots go to Pictures/ClaudeShot in your gallery.
Drag the button to move it. Drag it onto ✕ at the bottom to turn it off.
Prefer Power + Volume down? Turn on Phone screenshot buttons and those screenshots open here too.
Some phones close apps that run in the background. In App info, open Battery and choose “Unrestricted” or “Allow background activity”. ClaudeShot turns itself back on after a restart.
Your screenshots stay on your phone unless you share them. ClaudeShot has no internet access.
Tap the floating button to take a screenshot.
Screenshots you take with your phone buttons open in ClaudeShot.
Tap the floating button, or use your phone’s screenshot buttons.
Tap to edit and share it.
ClaudeShot is off. Open the app to turn it back on.
Floating button is off. Screenshots from your phone buttons still open in ClaudeShot.
The screenshot came out black. Some apps block screenshots. Otherwise, tap the button again.
Couldn’t take the screenshot. Try again.
ClaudeShot needs screen capture to take screenshots. Tap the button and choose “Start now”.
Copied. Paste it into any app.
Couldn’t save the image. Try again.
This screenshot is no longer available.
You haven’t saved, copied or shared it yet.
Your phone already saved the original screenshot. Your changes aren’t saved yet.
